A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sparse-autoencoder study of entity recognition and hallucinations. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. Existing Appendices A–P can be matched, and v2 adds Appendices Q–S.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gemma experiments measuring latent activations, refusal steering, activation patching, attention effects and error prediction, including supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama replication, post-cutoff song evaluation, controlled attention comparisons and token-likelihood analyses.

M1.justification: The latent-discovery criteria, activation steering, weight orthogonalization and uncertainty-latent selection procedures remain unchanged in Sections 2–7. The Llama experiments apply the existing framework; no new proposed algorithmic component, architecture or loss is documented.

E1.justification: The four Wikidata entity categories, attributes and dataset counts remain unchanged in Table 3. Section 4 and Appendix R add 283 song titles released after the stated August 2024 cutoff, introducing a limited temporal test population within the existing song domain.

E2.justification: Appendix M adds matched random-SAE-latent comparators to its aggregate attention-effect analysis. v1 already used random latents in other comparisons, including Appendix K, but did not report these Appendix M comparisons. The original refusal baselines remain, and the Llama replication uses the same comparator families.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental configurations through Llama 3.1 8B and LlamaScope, including 100-query known- and unknown-entity refusal evaluations and attention steering with coefficient 20. It also introduces matched-control attention tests on 100 prompts and FineWeb token-probability correlation procedures. These are additional evaluation designs rather than demonstrated changes to the original Gemma experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix R adds post-cutoff validation, while Appendix S directly investigates token predictability as an alternative explanation, including conditional probabilities, surrounding-token perplexity and prediction entropy. Appendix M adds controlled comparisons of attention effects. These substantially strengthen diagnostic analysis beyond v1's retained patching, steering and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: v2 adds directional t-tests comparing attention effects against ten matched random latents and reports correlation coefficients with p-values in Appendix S. v1 had descriptive error bars and t-statistics for latent selection, but lacked these inferential analyses. Figures 3 and 11 also newly identify the mean and standard deviation over the already reported ten random latents; this does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial Llama, temporal-validation and correlation results and revises Appendix M attention plots. Table 8 reports known/unknown activation rates of 6%/53%, 22%/55% and 13.4%/76% for Gemma 2 2B, Gemma 2 9B and Llama respectively. Appendix Q reports that known-latent steering does not reduce Llama refusals. The existing classifier's 73.2 AUROC and 72 F1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for SAEs, separation scores, latent selection, steering, orthogonalization and patching remain unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation is added. The new conditional-probability discussion supports empirical diagnostics rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The principal entity-recognition, refusal, attention and uncertainty contributions remain. v2 qualifies the self-knowledge interpretation as suggested knowledge awareness and adds a conclusion-level claim that the discovery methodology generalizes to other binary and continuous features. These adjust claim scope without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive caveats about entity-label errors and possible pretraining overlap in post-cutoff song titles. Section 6 proposes attention-key computation as a mechanism, and Appendix S develops the token-likelihood alternative and interprets small correlations as evidence against it. The replication discussion also exposes model-specific limits, including weak Gemma 2 9B unknown-latent effects and unsuccessful Llama refusal reduction.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link for the study's code, identifies LlamaScope resources and documents the Llama attention-steering coefficient. Section 7 newly specifies the 50%/10%/40% prompt split and training-set t-statistic calculation. These improve documentation; the added split details do not establish that the original experiment changed or was rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Yu et al. (2023), He et al. (2024) and Joshi et al. (2024), and connects uncertainty directions to prior pre-generation truthfulness probes. The overall research positioning remains stable. Cunningham-to-Huben and other publication updates refer to existing works rather than new research additions.

P1.justification: The nine-section main structure and existing appendix organization are retained. v2 adds Appendices Q–S, short explanatory passages and qualifications, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments and conference headers. Most existing methodological and results prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Appendix M charts are redrawn with revised head ranges, less crowded tick labels, changed scales and expanded captions. New Llama panels, probability histograms and Tables 8–9 substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing graphics are largely retained or relocated; for example, v1 Figures 20–22 correspond to v2 Figures 22–24.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence previously concentrated in Gemma through cross-family replication, post-cutoff validation and controlled attention tests, while directly examining token predictability as an alternative explanation. More explicit labeling caveats and model-specific failures improve the calibration of its conclusions. A localized inconsistency remains between Figure 28 and Table 9's Gemma 2 2B activation frequencies, but the added validation and clearer limits provide a substantial net improvement.
